  <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><a id="notes" title="notes" href="#"></a>NOTES TO COND</b><b>ENSED CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b><b> (UNAUDITED)</b></p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfPresentationAndSignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3185978" escape="true">
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> </b><b>Basis of Presentation</b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>General</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">First Community Bankshares, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;), a financial holding company, was founded in <em style="font: inherit;">1989</em> and reincorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia. The Company&#8217;s principal executive office is located in Bluefield, Virginia. The Company provides banking products and services to individual and commercial customers through its wholly owned subsidiary First Community Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), a Virginia-chartered banking institution founded in <em style="font: inherit;">1874.</em> The Bank offers wealth management and investment advice through its Trust Division and wholly owned subsidiary First Community Wealth Management.&#160; Unless the context suggests otherwise, the terms &#8220;First Community,&#8221; &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; and &#8220;us&#8221; refer to First Community Bankshares, Inc. and its subsidiaries as a consolidated entity.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="c145258893" escape="true"><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Principles of Consolidation</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company&#8217;s accounting and reporting policies conform with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) for interim financial information and with the instructions to Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-Q and Rule <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">01</em> of Regulation S-<em style="font: inherit;">X.</em> Accordingly, they do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> include all of the information and footnotes required by U.S. GAAP for complete financial statements. The consolidated financial statements include all accounts of the Company and its wholly owned subsidiaries and eliminate all intercompany balances and transactions. The Company operates in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> business segment, Community Banking, which consists of all operations, including commercial and consumer banking, lending activities, and wealth management. Operating results for interim periods are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily indicative of results that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be expected for other interim periods or for the full year. In management&#8217;s opinion, the accompanying unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements contain all necessary adjustments, including normal recurring accruals, and disclosures for a fair presentation.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">These unaudited interim condensed consolidated financial statements should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes included in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K for the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> (the &#8220;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K&#8221;), as filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the &#8220;SEC&#8221;) on <em style="font: inherit;"> March 6, 2026. </em>The condensed consolidated balance sheet as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, has been derived from the audited consolidated financial statements.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:PriorPeriodReclassificationAdjustmentDescription" id="c145258894" escape="true"><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Reclassifications</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Certain amounts reported in prior years have been reclassified to conform to the current year&#8217;s presentation. These reclassifications had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> effect on the Company&#8217;s results of operations, financial position, or net cash flow.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&#160;</b></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c145258895" escape="true"><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Use of Estimates</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Preparation of the condensed consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities as of the date of the balance sheet and reported amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Significant Accounting Policies</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">The Company&#8217;s significant accounting policies as presented&#160;in Note <em style="font: inherit;">1,</em> &#8220;Basis of Presentation and Significant Accounting Policies,&#8221; of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements in Part II, Item <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> of the Company&#8217;s </span><em style="font: inherit;">2025</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> Form <em style="font: inherit;">10</em>-K remain unchanged except for the following recent accounting standards adopted described below.</span></p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c145258896" escape="true"><p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Recent Accounting </i></b><b><i>Standards</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">
    <i>Standards Adopted</i>
   </div>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> &#8220;Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>).&#8221; The amendments in this ASU are related to the rate reconciliation and income taxes paid disclosures and are designed to improve the transparency of income tax disclosures by requiring (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) consistent categories and greater disaggregation of information in the rate reconciliation and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) income taxes paid disaggregated by jurisdiction. The ASU was effective for annual periods beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025, </em>and was&#160;applied on a prospective basis.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material impact on the Consolidated Financial Statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08,</em> "Financial Instruments- Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Purchased Loans".&#160; The amendment simplifies accounting for acquired loans under the current expected credit losses (CECL) model by expanding use of the gross-up method to a new category of purchased seasonal loans (PSLs).&#160; &#160;PSLs are acquired loans purchased more than <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days after origination or acquired in a business combination.&#160; For PSLs, an allowance for credit loss is to be recorded at acquisition with an equal increase to amortized cost and remove credit loss expense on acquisition date.&#160; The ASU does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> apply to credit cards, Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> trade receivables, and debt securities.&#160; ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> requires entities to apply the amendments prospectively to loans acquired on or after the initial application date and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> require retrospective restatement of prior periods.&#160; The amendments in this update are effective for annual periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>an early adoption is permitted for annual financial statements that have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> yet been issued or made available.&#160; The Company early adopted the provisions of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> in connection with its merger of Hometown Bancshares, Inc., which was completed on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 23, 2026.&#160; </em>The Company applied the guidance prospectively to loans acquired in the transaction and will apply the guidance to any subsequent acquisitions occurring on or after initial adoption.&#160; Due to&#160;the adoption of&#160;the standard the&#160;Company was <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> required to recognize a $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241723" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_AdjustmentsForNewAccountingPronouncementsAxis-AccountingStandardsUpdate202508Member" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLossPurchasedWithCreditDeteriorationIncrease" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2.98</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;provision expense that would otherwise have been recorded.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Standards <em style="font: inherit;">Not</em> Yet Adopted&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> "Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">230</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses". The amendment requires disclosure of disaggregated information about specific expense categories underlying certain income statement expense line items.&#160; The guidance is effective for the Company for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>and interim reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027.&#160; </em>Accordingly, the Company expects to adopt the standard in its annual financial statements for the year ending <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2027, </em>and in interim periods beginning in fiscal year <em style="font: inherit;">2028.</em></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05,</em> "Financial Instruments- Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets".&#160; This&#160;amendment introduces a practical expedient available to all entities that permits an entity to assume that existing economic conditions at&#160;the balance sheet date will persist for the remaining life of current accounts receivable and current contract assets, rather than developing a full forward-looking forecast.&#160; This ASU will become effective for the Company in <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> on a prospective basis.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> "Derivatives and Hedging (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>): Targeted Improvements to Hedge Accounting".&#160; The amendment amends ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em> to clarify, improve, and better align hedge accounting guidance with entities' economic risk management strategies and address implementation challenges in practice.&#160; The ASU is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>with early adoption permitted.&#160; &#160;The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> "Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>): Narrow-Scope Improvements".&#160; The amendment is to enhance the clarity, navigability, and application of interim reporting guidance in ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em> without expanding or reducing the fundamental nature of the interim reporting framework.&#160; The amendments clarify when interim guidance applies, the form and content of interim financial statements, and the related disclosure requirements under GAAP.&#160; The ASU is effective for periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>with early adoption permitted.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12,</em> "Codification Improvements".&#160; The amendment consists of technical corrections, clarifications, and narrow-scope improvements that address unintended application issues and improve the clarity and usability of GAAP without making substantive changes to current accounting practice.&#160; The amendments are intended to reduce diversity in practice and correct errors or ambiguous provisions in the Codification.&#160; The ASU is effective for periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>with early adoption permitted.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect other recent accounting standards issued by the FASB or other standards-setting bodies to have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em>&#160; Acquisitions and Divestitures</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> January 23, 2026 (</em>the "Effective Time"),&#160;the Company completed its previously announced merger (the &#8220;Merger&#8221;) with Hometown Bancshares, Inc. a West Virginia corporation headquartered in Middlebourne, West Virginia (&#8220;Hometown&#8221;), pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the &#8220;Agreement&#8221;) dated <em style="font: inherit;"> July 19, 2025, </em>by and between the company&#160;and Hometown.&#160; At the Effective Time, Hometown merged with and into the Company, with the Company&#160;as the surviving corporation in the Merger.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Immediately following the Merger, Union Bank, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hometown, merged with and into First Community Bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company&#160;(the &#8220;Bank Merger&#8221;), with First Community Bank as the surviving bank in the Bank Merger.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Pursuant to the Agreement,&#160;each outstanding share of common stock of Hometown was converted into the right to receive <ix:nonFraction id="c145241773" contextRef="i_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:BusinessCombinationStockConversionRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.706</ix:nonFraction> shares (the &#8220;Exchange Ratio&#8221;) of the Company's&#160;common stock, par value $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241774" contextRef="i_2026-01-23" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction> per share, plus cash, without interest, in lieu of fractional shares.&#160; In connection with the transaction, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c145241775" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,029,314</ix:nonFraction> common shares.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Under the terms of the Agreement, all Hometown stock appreciation rights under a stock appreciation award (except certain stock appreciation rights that were unvested as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025) </em>and all Hometown dividend equivalent rights granted under the Hometown Dividend Equivalent Incentive Plan that were outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, to the extent <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> vested, became fully vested, and were canceled. The holders of stock appreciation rights received a cash&#160; payment equal to the number determined by multiplying (i) the excess, if any of (A) Average Closing Price (as defined in the Agreement) multiplied by (B) the Exchange Ratio over the applicable exercise price of the stock appreciation right, by (ii) the number of shares of Hometown common stock subject to the applicable stock appreciation right. The holders of dividend equivalent rights received a cash payment equal to the account value of the applicable dividend rights award. The stock appreciation rights that are unvested as of <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025, </em>were assumed by the Company.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The transaction was accounted for using the acquisition method of accounting and, accordingly, assets acquired, liabilities assumed and consideration exchanged were recorded at estimated fair value on the acquisition date.&#160; Fair values are preliminary and subject to refinement for up to a year after the closing date of the acquisition.&#160; The Company incurred a total of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241777" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">5.22</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;in merger expenses related to the Hometown transaction,&#160;$<ix:nonFraction id="c145241778" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2.91</ix:nonFraction> million was recorded in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> and $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241780" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2.31</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter of <em style="font: inherit;">2026.</em>&#160; These costs were primarily related to data conversion, investment banking fees, and legal fees.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Goodwill arising from business combinations represents the excess of the purchase price over the sum of the estimated fair values of the tangible and identifiable intangible assets acquired less the fair value of the liabilities assumed.&#160; The Hometown acquisition resulted in the Company recognizing $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241783" contextRef="i_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Goodwill" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.73</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;in goodwill.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The primary identifiable intangible asset we typically record in connection with a whole bank or bank branch acquisition is the value of the core deposit intangibles which represents the estimated value of the long-term deposit relationships acquired in the transaction.&#160; Determining the amount of&#160;identifiable intangible assets and their average lives involves multiple assumptions and estimates and is typically determined by performing a discounted cash flow analysis, which involves a combination of any or all of the following assumptions:&#160; customer attrition/runoff, alternative funding costs, deposit servicing costs, and discount rates.&#160; The core deposit intangibles are amortized over the estimated useful lives of the deposit accounts based on a method that we believe reasonably approximates the anticipated benefit stream from this intangible.&#160; Core deposit intangibles for the Hometown transaction totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241785" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember_FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis-CoreDepositsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinitelivedIntangibleAssetsAcquired1" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">8.59</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">When loans are acquired, due to the adoption of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08</em> in conjunction with ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13</em> (CECL), the Company classifies acquired loans as either purchased credit deteriorated (&#8220;PCD&#8221;), purchased seasoned loans (&#8220;PSL&#8221;), or other non-PCD loans at the acquisition date. PCD loans, representing assets with more-than-insignificant credit deterioration since origination, and PSL loans, which meet the criteria for application of the gross-up approach under the new guidance, are both recorded by recognizing an allowance for credit losses as an adjustment to the amortized cost basis of the loans at acquisition, resulting in <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> initial impact to earnings. Subsequent changes in expected credit losses for these loans are recognized through provision expense in the periods in which they occur. Loans that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> meet the definition of PCD or PSL are recorded at fair value, typically determined using a discounted cash flow methodology incorporating assumptions such as discount rates, expected lives, prepayments, probability of default, and loss given default, with any resulting discount accreted into interest income over the estimated remaining life of the loans. An allowance for credit losses on these non-PCD loans is recognized through provision expense in the period of acquisition. This framework aligns the accounting for acquired loans more closely with their underlying credit characteristics while reducing earnings volatility at acquisition.&#160; The fair value of purchased loans with credit deterioration was $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241792" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivablePurchasedWithCreditDeteriorationAmountAtPurchasePrice" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">11.05</ix:nonFraction> million on the date of acquisition with the gross contractual amount totaling $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241793" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivablePurchasedWithCreditDeteriorationAmountAtParValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">12.66</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160; &#160;Purchased seasoned loans&#160;acquired had a fair value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241794" contextRef="i_2026-01-23_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-PurchasedSeasonedLoanMember_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquiredReceivablesFairValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">159.77</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million with a gross contractual value of $<ix:nonFraction id="c145241795" contextRef="i_2026-01-23_AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis-PurchasedSeasonedLoanMember_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesIncMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquiredReceivablesGrossContractualAmount" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">161.58</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">There were <ix:nonFraction id="c145241920" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionNumberOfPositions" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">87</ix:nonFraction>&#160;individual debt securities in an unrealized loss position as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and the combined depreciation in value&#160;represented&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145241921" contextRef="i_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:PercentageOfCombinedDepreciationOfCombinedReportedValueOfAggregateSecuritiesPortfolio" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.93</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;of the debt securities portfolio. There were&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145241922" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleUnrealizedLossPositionNumberOfPositions" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">85</ix:nonFraction>&#160;individual debt securities in an unrealized loss position as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, and their combined depreciation in value represented&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c145241923" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:PercentageOfCombinedDepreciationOfCombinedReportedValueOfAggregateSecuritiesPortfolio" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">7.83</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;of&#160;the debt securities portfolio.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Management evaluates securities for impairment where there has been a decline in fair value below the amortized cost basis of a security to determine whether there is a credit loss associated with the decline in fair value on at least a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market concerns warrant such evaluation. Credit losses are calculated individually, rather than collectively, using a discounted cash flow method, whereby management compares the present value of expected cash flows with the amortized cost basis of the security.&#160; The credit loss component would be recognized through the provision for credit losses and the creation of an allowance for credit losses. Consideration is given to (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer including looking at default and delinquency rates, (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;the outlook for receiving the contractual cash flows of the investments, (<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>)&#160;the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, (<em style="font: inherit;">4</em>)&#160;our intent and ability to retain its investment in the issuer for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value or for a debt security whether it is more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that we will be required to sell the debt security prior to recovering its fair value, (<em style="font: inherit;">5</em>)&#160;the anticipated outlook for changes in the general level of interest rates, (<em style="font: inherit;">6</em>) credit ratings, (<em style="font: inherit;">7</em>) <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party guarantees, and (<em style="font: inherit;">8</em>) collateral values. In analyzing an issuer&#8217;s financial condition, management considers whether the securities are issued by the federal government or its agencies, whether downgrades by bond rating agencies have occurred, the results of reviews of the issuer&#8217;s financial condition, and the issuer&#8217;s anticipated ability to pay the contractual cash flows of the investments. &#160;All of the U.S. Treasury and Agency-Backed Securities have the full faith and credit backing of the United State Government or <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> of its agencies. Municipal securities and all other securities that do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a <em style="font: inherit;">zero</em> expected credit loss are evaluated quarterly to determine whether there is a credit loss associated with a decline in fair value. All debt securities available-for-sale in an unrealized loss position as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, continue to perform as scheduled and we do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> believe that there is a credit loss or that a provision for credit losses is necessary. Also, as part of our evaluation of our intent and ability to hold investments for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in the market, we consider our investment strategy, cash flow needs, liquidity position, capital adequacy and interest rate risk position. We do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> currently intend to sell the securities within the portfolio, and it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that we will be required to sell the debt securities.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Management continues to monitor all of our securities with a high degree of scrutiny. There can be <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> assurance that we will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> conclude in future periods that conditions existing at that time indicate some or all of its securities <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be sold or would require a charge to earnings as a provision for credit losses in such periods.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivablesTextBlock" id="c3185990" escape="true">
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">5</em></b><b>. Credit Quality</b><b> </b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company uses a risk grading matrix to assign a risk grade to each loan in its portfolio. Loan risk ratings <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be upgraded or downgraded to reflect current information identified during the loan review process. The general characteristics of each risk grade are as follows:</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Pass -- This grade is assigned to loans with acceptable credit quality and risk. The Company further segments this grade based on borrower characteristics that include capital strength, earnings stability, liquidity, leverage, and industry conditions.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Special Mention -- This grade is assigned to loans that require an above average degree of supervision and attention. These loans have the characteristics of an asset with acceptable credit quality and risk; however, adverse economic or financial conditions exist that create potential weaknesses deserving of management&#8217;s close attention. If potential weaknesses are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected, the prospect of repayment <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>worsen.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Substandard -- This grade is assigned to loans that have well defined weaknesses that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>make payment default, or principal exposure, possible. These loans will likely be dependent on collateral liquidation, secondary repayment sources, or events outside the normal course of business to meet repayment terms.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Doubtful -- This grade is assigned to loans that have the weaknesses inherent in substandard loans; however, the weaknesses are so severe that collection or liquidation in full is unlikely based on current facts, conditions, and values. Due to certain specific pending factors, the amount of loss cannot yet be determined.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Loss -- This grade is assigned to loans that will be charged off or charged down when payments, including the timing and value of payments, are uncertain. This risk grade does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> imply that the asset has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> recovery or salvage value, but simply means that it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practical or desirable to defer writing off, either all or a portion of, the loan balance even though partial recovery <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be realized in the future.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Loans are considered past due when either principal or interest payments become contractually delinquent by <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> days or more. The Company&#8217;s policy is to discontinue the accrual of interest, if warranted, on loans based on the payment status, evaluation of the related collateral, and the financial strength of the borrower. Loans that are <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days or more past due are placed on nonaccrual status. Management <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>elect to continue the accrual of interest when the loan is well secured and in process of collection. When interest accruals are discontinued, interest accrued and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> collected in the current year is reversed from income, and interest accrued and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> collected from prior years is charged to the allowance for credit losses. Nonaccrual loans <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be returned to accrual status when all principal and interest amounts contractually due, including past due payments, are brought current&#894; the ability of the borrower to repay the obligation is reasonably assured&#894; and there is generally a period of at least <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months of repayment performance by the borrower in accordance with the contractual terms. There was <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> material nonaccrual loan interest recognized in income during the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em>&#160;quarter&#160;of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2026</em>&#160;or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>.&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The following tables presents the aging of past due loans, by loan class, as of the dates indicated. Nonaccrual loans <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> days or more past due are included in the applicable delinquency category:&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">ASC <em style="font: inherit;">326</em> prescribes that when an entity determines foreclosure is probable, the expected credit loss can&#160;be measured based on the fair value of the collateral. As a practical expedient, an entity <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>use the fair value as of the reporting date when recording the net carrying amount of the asset. For the collateral dependent asset ("CDA") a credit loss expense is recorded for loan amounts in excess of fair value of the collateral.&#160; The Company had <ix:nonFraction id="c145242341" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:CollateralDependentLoans" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> collateral-dependent loans as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026&#160;</em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3186019" escape="true">
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">9</em></b><b>. Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Generally, derivative instruments help the Company manage exposure to market risk and meet customer financing needs. Market risk represents the possibility that fluctuations in external factors such as interest rates, market-driven loan rates, prices, or other economic factors will adversely affect economic value or net interest income.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company has used&#160;interest rate swap contracts to modify its exposure to interest rate risk caused by changes in benchmark interest rates&#160;in relation to certain designated fixed rate loans.&#160; These instruments are used to convert these fixed rate loans to an effective floating rate. If the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") plus a spread&#160;falls below the loan&#8217;s stated fixed rate for a given period, the Company will owe the floating rate payer the notional amount times the difference between the floating rate&#160;and the stated fixed rate. If SOFR&#160;is above the stated rate for a given period, the Company will receive payments based on the notional amount times the difference between the floating rate&#160;and the stated fixed rate.&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company's interest rate swaps qualify as fair value hedging instruments; therefore, fair value changes in the derivative and hedged item attributable to the hedged risk are recognized in earnings in the same period. The fair value hedges were effective as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026</em>, and <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following table presents the notional, or contractual, amounts and fair values of derivative instruments as of the dates indicated:</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">10</em></b><b>. </b><b>Employee </b><b>Benefit Plans </b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company maintains <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> nonqualified domestic, noncontributory defined benefit plans (the &#8220;Benefit Plans&#8221;) for key members of senior management and non-management directors. The Company&#8217;s unfunded Benefit Plans include the Supplemental Executive Retention Plan ("SERP")&#160;and the Directors&#8217; Supplemental Retirement Plan ("Director Plan").   <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementInputsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3186030" escape="true">
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">13</em></b><b>. Fair Value </b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Financial Instruments Measured at Fair Value</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants. The fair value hierarchy ranks the inputs used in measuring fair value as follows:</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> &#8211; Observable, unadjusted quoted prices in active markets</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8211; Inputs other than quoted prices included in Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> that are directly or indirectly observable for the asset or liability</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width: 18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top;"> <p style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8211; Unobservable inputs with little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market activity that require the Company to use reasonable inputs and assumptions</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company uses fair value measurements to record adjustments to certain financial assets and liabilities on a recurring basis. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required to record certain assets at fair value on a nonrecurring basis in specific circumstances, such as evidence of impairment. Methodologies used to determine fair value might be highly subjective and judgmental in nature; therefore, valuations <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be precise. If the Company determines that a valuation technique change is necessary, the change is assumed to have occurred at the end of the respective reporting period. The following discussion describes the valuation methodologies used for instruments measured at fair value, as well as the general classification of such instruments under the valuation hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>
    <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell PGNUM" style="text-align: center; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;;">
       <em style="font: inherit;">32</em>
      </div>
     </div>
    </div>
    <hr style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; border: none; width: 100%; height: 2px; color: #000000; background-color: #000000"/>
    <div class="PGHDR" style="text-align: left; width: 100%">
     <div class="hf-row">
      <div class="hf-cell TOCLink" style="display: inline-block; text-align: left;">
       <a href="#toc" style="font-weight: initial; font-style: initial; font-variant: initial; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Table of Contents</a>
      </div>
     </div>
    </div>
   </ix:exclude>
   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);"><i>Assets and Liabilities Reported at Fair Value on a Recurring Basis</i></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i style="font-size: 10pt;">Available-for-sale </i><i style="font-size: 10pt;">Debt </i><i style="font-size: 10pt;">Securities</i></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <div style="font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">
     Debt securities available-for-sale are reported at fair value on a recurring basis. The fair value of Level
    <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> securities is based on quoted market prices in active markets, if available. If quoted market prices are
    <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are measured utilizing independent valuation techniques of identical or similar securities for which significant assumptions are primarily derived from or corroborated by observable market data. Level
    <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> securities use fair value measurements from independent pricing services obtained by the Company. These fair value measurements consider observable data that
    <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include dealer quotes, market spreads, cash flows, the Treasury yield curve, live trading levels, trade execution data, market consensus prepayment speeds, credit information, and bond terms and conditions. The Company&#8217;s Level
    <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> securities include U.S. Agency and Treasury securities, municipal securities, and mortgage-backed securities. Securities are based on Level
    <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs when there is limited activity or less transparency to the valuation inputs. In the absence of observable or corroborated market data, internally developed estimates that incorporate market-based assumptions are used when such information is available.
   </div>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">Fair value models <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required when trading activity has declined significantly or does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exist, prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> current, or pricing variations are significant. For Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> securities, the Company obtains the cash flow of specific securities from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties that use modeling software to determine cash flows based on market participant data and knowledge of the structures of each individual security. The fair values of Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> securities are determined by applying proper market observable discount rates to the cash flow derived from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party models. &#160;Securities with increased uncertainty about the receipt of cash flows are discounted at higher rates due to the addition of a deal specific credit premium based on assumptions about the performance of the underlying collateral. Finally, internal fair value model pricing and external pricing observations are combined by assigning weights to each pricing observation. Pricing is reviewed for reasonableness based on the direction of specific markets and the general economic indicators.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Equity Securities.</i> Equity securities are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis and included in other assets in the consolidated balance sheets. The Company uses Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs to value equity securities that are traded in active markets. Equity securities that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> actively traded are classified in Level <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Loans Held for Investment</i>. Loans held for investment that are subject to a fair value hedge are reported at fair value derived from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party models. Loans&#160;designated in&#160;fair value hedges are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Deferred Compensation Assets and Liabilities</i>. Securities held for trading purposes are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis and included in other assets in the consolidated balance sheets. These securities include assets related to employee deferred compensation plans, which are generally invested in Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> equity securities. The liability associated with these deferred compensation plans is carried at the fair value of the obligation to the employee, which corresponds to the fair value of the invested assets.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);"><i>Derivative Assets and Liabilities</i>. Derivatives are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis. The Company obtains dealer quotes, Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs, based on observable data to value derivatives.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">The following tables summarize financial assets and liabilities recorded at fair value on a recurring basis, by the level of valuation inputs in the fair value hierarchy, as of the dates indicated:</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);"><i>Assets Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis</i></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><i>Collateral Dependent Loans and OREO:&#160; </i>The<i>&#160;</i>Fair value of collateral dependent loans and OREO&#160;is&#160;measured&#160;on a nonrecurring basis using Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs, which typically include appraised values of collateral, adjusted for estimated selling costs and other qualitative factors. The Company had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> collateral-dependent loans or OREO measured at fair value on a nonrecurring basis as of <em style="font: inherit;"> March 31, 2026 </em>or <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255);">&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3186035" escape="true">
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">14</em></b><b>. </b><b>Litigation, Commitments</b><b>,</b><b> and Contingencies</b><b> </b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Litigation</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">We are currently a defendant in&#160;legal actions and asserted claims in the normal course of business. Although we are unable to assess the ultimate outcome of each matter with certainty, we believe that the resolution of these actions should <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Commitments and Contingencies</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Company is a party to financial instruments with off balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit, standby letters of credit, and financial guarantees. These instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk beyond the amount recognized in the consolidated balance sheets. The contractual amounts of these instruments reflect the extent of involvement the Company has in particular classes of financial instruments. If the other party to a financial instrument does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> perform, the Company&#8217;s credit loss exposure is the same as the contractual amount of the instrument. The Company uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for on balance sheet instruments.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> violation of any condition established in the contract. Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>require payment of a fee. Since many commitments are expected to expire without being drawn on, the total commitment amounts do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent future cash requirements. The amount of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary, is based on management&#8217;s credit evaluation of each customer on a case-by-case basis. Collateral <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include accounts receivable, inventory, property, plant and equipment, and income producing commercial properties. The Company maintains a reserve for the risk inherent in unfunded lending commitments, which is included in other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">Standby letters of credit and financial guarantees are conditional commitments issued by the Company to guarantee the performance of a customer to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. The credit risk involved in issuing letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved in extending credit to customers. The amount of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary, to secure the customer&#8217;s performance under certain letters of credit is based on management&#8217;s credit evaluation of the customer.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">The following table presents the off-balance sheet financial instruments as of the dates indicated:</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">15.</em> Segment Information</b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company conducts its business activities through community banking. Community banking revolves around serving the community and customers where the bank has branches and offices. Community banking consists of commercial and consumer banking, lending activities, and wealth management.&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s chief executive officer is in charge of allocating the Company&#8217;s resources and assessing the Company's performance, and as such, has been identified as the chief operating decision maker. The chief operating decision maker regularly reviews a multitude of reports that have a varying level of combined detail on products offered, however, all of the information and activity reviewed fall under the definition of community banking.</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Based on the business activities and information reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, the Company has <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> reportable segment - Community Banking.&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The accounting policies of the community banking segment are the same as those for the Company described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em> In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">280,</em> the Company has concluded that consolidated net income is the measure of segment profit or loss that is required to be reported because it is the measure determined in accordance with measurement principles that are most consistent with US GAAP. As the Company only has <ix:nonFraction id="c145245179" contextRef="d_2026-01-01_2026-03-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">one</ix:nonFraction> reportable segment, total segment net income and total segment assets are equivalent to the results disclosed in the accompanying Consolidated Statements of Income and Consolidated Balance Sheets, respectively.</p>
